sara: heads-up - hit a nasty hang when cancelling a typed async-wrapper around client.stream(). seems to swallow aclose and keeps the connection half-alive on the server. repro attached. :bug:

sara: repro summary: typed wrapper declared as -> AsyncIterator[bytes], mid-stream 401 triggers refresh, user breaks out of consumer loop, but server still shows connection ESTABLISHED and next request stalls with partial payload.

sara: short repro:
```python
from typing import AsyncIterator

async def transform(src: AsyncIterator[bytes]) -> AsyncIterator[bytes]:
    async for part in src:
        yield part.replace(b"foo", b"bar")

# consumer
async for chunk in transform(client.stream("/v1/generate")):
    if stop_condition:
        break
```

taylor: do you see the SDK call its own aclose() on cancel? or is it not reached?

sara: SDK does call its internal generator.aclose(), but because the wrapper is a proxy object produced by a typing helper in our codebase, the wrapper object lacks __anext__/aclose forwarding, so the internal gen never gets closed.

ryan: hmm, interesting. sounds like two issues: (1) wrappers must preserve the async iterator protocol (including aclose/athrow), and (2) SDK should defensively call aclose on inner object even if proxy is weird.

sara: agreed. quick fix on customer code was to add try/finally in wrapper:
```python
async def transform(src: AsyncIterator[bytes]) -> AsyncIterator[bytes]:
    try:
        async for p in src:
            yield p
    finally:
        await src.aclose()
```

alex: can you confirm this happens with chunked SSE too, not only gRPC/transport?
sara: yes, reprobed with SSE chunked server and identical behavior. server socket remains open, our KV cache prefix isn't evicted.

taylor: can you add a small unit test that simulates a 401 mid-stream and asserts aclose() was awaited? will help triage.

sara: adding test now. PR incoming with test + docs note about wrapper patterns.

ryan: can SDK implement a safety: if underlying generator has aclose attribute but wrapper lacks it, attempt to poke gen via getattr to call aclose on cancellation? might be messy but pragmatic.

alex: also plz check Trio/anyio wrappers — I saw a crash when aclose raised CancelledError. we should swallow CancelledError from aclose and still close the socket.

devex-bot: issue opened #3507 "py-sdk: wrapper proxies can drop aclose -> streaming cancel leak" (https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/issues/3507)

sara: tagging eng-runtime + devex for visibility. if someone wants to pair on a short fix tomorrow ping me. :hammer_and_wrench:

ryan: assigning to eng-ml/devex to add unit + minimal runtime fallback. thanks for clear repro!
